DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 10) Apologetics

Q1. Which pair of questions does the lesson associate with the biographical test?
A. How many authors produced the document, and how many people witnessed the events described in it?
B. How many manuscripts are available and whether their contents are the same or similar, and how long the interval is between the original and earliest available manuscript?
C. Whether archaeology supports the document, and whether later communities accepted the document as authoritative?
D. Whether the document contains prophecy, and whether the prophecy was fulfilled within the period it describes?
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson assesses manuscript evidence by considering the number and similarity of manuscripts and the interval from the original to the earliest available copies.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — approx. 01:37–06:01

Q2. What does the lesson mean by saying, "A dead God cannot give eternal life"?
A. Eternal life depends on Jesus having conquered death rather than remaining under the power of death.
B. Eternal life can only be received by those who physically witness Jesus' resurrection.
C. Eternal life is possible only when believers are able to prove the resurrection through historical documents.
D. Eternal life depends on believers becoming physically immortal before they can receive salvation.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects Jesus’ resurrection with believers’ redemption and future resurrection.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — 04:03–05:02

Q3. What does the internal evidence test examine?
A. Whether archaeological discoveries confirm the locations and events described within the Bible.
B. Whether writings outside the Bible confirm the people, places and events described within the Bible.
C. Whether the information within the Bible is coherent and free from known contradictions.
D. Whether the Bible contains more surviving manuscripts than other ancient documents from the same period.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines the internal evidence test as examining the Bible’s own testimony for coherence and known contradictions.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 06:41–07:44

Q4. Why does the lesson describe the resurrection as more than simply getting the facts of the past right?
A. It establishes a guarantee concerning the future of those who believe in Jesus.
B. It establishes that every historical detail concerning Jesus can now be independently verified.
C. It establishes that believers will never experience suffering or death after becoming Christians.
D. It establishes that every person who hears the gospel will automatically receive eternal life.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents Jesus’ resurrection as assurance that believers will rise as well.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — 04:03–05:46

Q5. Why does the lesson refer to Isaiah's writings about Jesus?
A. Isaiah was written during Jesus' lifetime and records eyewitness testimony about His ministry.
B. Isaiah was discovered as part of the earliest complete New Testament manuscript and confirms the Gospel accounts.
C. Isaiah contains predictions about Jesus' life and death that were written over 700 years before Jesus was born and were later fulfilled.
D. Isaiah proves that Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote their Gospel accounts together from the same source.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson cites Isaiah’s predictions about Jesus’ life and death as prophecies written centuries before his birth and later fulfilled.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 10:31–11:39

Q6. Why does the lesson regard the fact that women were the first witnesses of the empty tomb as significant evidence?
A. Women were considered the most reliable legal witnesses in the first-century Jewish world.
B. Women were treated as highly respected public authorities whose testimony was preferred over that of men.
C. Women were treated as second-class citizens in that cultural context, making their inclusion as first witnesses an unlikely choice if the story were fabricated to be convincing.
D. Women were the only people permitted to enter tombs and were automatically considered reliable witnesses.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson argues that reporting women as the first witnesses would have been an unlikely choice for a fabricated account.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD IV — approx. 06:51–09:42

Q7. Which statement best captures the idea that what appears evil or chaotic may not be ultimate?
A. If an event eventually produces something good, the original event should no longer be regarded as evil.
B. If God has a purpose, every event must have been directly caused by Him.
C. A painful or chaotic reality can be genuinely difficult while still not representing the final outcome of God's purpose.
D. Human beings should stop judging circumstances because only God can determine whether something is good.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says present evil or chaos can be real without being the final outcome of God’s purpose.
REF: THEODICY II — 08:26–09:12

Q8. Why does the lesson consider Jesus' teaching about Himself from Scripture significant?
A. Because Jesus' use of Scripture proves that every surviving biblical manuscript has been preserved perfectly.
B. Because Jesus wrote the Old Testament Himself and could therefore explain every part of it from personal authorship.
C. Because Jesus' teaching about Scripture means that external evidence is no longer necessary for examining the Bible.
D. Because Jesus was the person prophesied about and could teach about Himself from the Scriptures that spoke about Him.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Jesus could teach about himself from the Scriptures that prophesied about him.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 10:31–11:39

Q9. What distinction does Hebrews 9 make between Christ's sacrifice and the sacrifices offered by the Old Testament high priest?
A. Christ entered the Most Holy Place repeatedly with His own blood, while the Old Testament high priest entered once a year with animal blood.
B. Christ entered the earthly sanctuary once with His own blood, while the Old Testament high priest entered the heavenly sanctuary repeatedly with animal blood.
C. Christ entered heaven once and for all by His own blood, while the Old Testament high priest repeatedly entered the Most Holy Place with the blood of animals.
D. Christ entered the Most Holy Place every year with His own blood, while the Old Testament high priest offered animal blood only once for Israel.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson contrasts the high priest’s repeated entry with animal blood and Christ’s once-for-all entry into heaven with his own blood.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — 00:15–02:35

Q10. A believer is suffering despite trusting God and wonders whether the suffering means Christ has failed to defeat evil. Which response best reflects the framework presented?
A. The suffering proves that Christ's victory applies only after death and has no present relevance.
B. The suffering shows that the believer has not yet exercised enough faith to appropriate Christ's victory.
C. The suffering exists within the present reality of a fallen world, while Christ's victory guarantees that suffering and death will not have the final word.
D. The suffering should be understood as God's direct method of teaching the believer whatever lesson they have not yet learned.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects present suffering with creation’s corruption and presents Christ’s victory as assurance that death and suffering will not have the final word.
REF: THEODICY IV — approx. 00:49–02:59; 14:42–18:23

Q11. What does the lesson mean when it says that the different parties in the Day of Atonement represented one person, Jesus?
A. It means that the high priest, the goats and the other elements were separate sacrifices that were eventually replaced by Jesus.
B. It means that the high priest and the goats were historical figures who physically became Jesus during His ministry.
C. It means that the different elements of the ceremony served as a type and shadow of what Jesus Christ would come to accomplish.
D. It means that Jesus performed the Day of Atonement ceremony in the same form before beginning His earthly ministry.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents the Day of Atonement’s elements as a type and shadow of what Jesus would accomplish.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD I — 12:06–13:42

Q12. What does the lesson mean when it describes money as a "spiritual stethoscope"?
A. The amount of money a person has reveals the level of spiritual maturity that person has attained.
B. The way a person responds to money and giving can reveal the condition of that person's heart.
C. The level of financial success a person experiences reveals the strength of that person's relationship with God.
D. The amount of money a person gives determines whether God accepts that person's faith and worship.
ANSWER: B
REF: Not found in the provided sources — N/A

Q13. Why has the problem addressed by theodicy continued to generate questions among Christians and non-Christians?
A. Because Scripture gives no examples of people questioning God's justice
B. Because the existence of evil creates questions about how God's goodness, power and justice relate to human experience
C. Because Christians have historically disagreed about whether God possesses absolute sovereignty
D. Because the Bible presents evil as a mystery that human beings are forbidden to investigate
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects the problem of evil with questions about God’s goodness, knowledge, power, and justice.
REF: THEODICY I — approx. 01:18–03:28

Q14. Why does the lesson argue that the Islamic substitution theory conflicts with the earliest historical testimony about Jesus?
A. Because the theory appeared several hundred years after the Christian accounts and conflicts with both Christian and non-Christian testimony concerning His crucifixion.
B. Because the theory appeared before the Christian accounts and therefore contradicts the eyewitnesses who recorded Jesus' crucifixion.
C. Because the theory was developed by Roman authorities who were attempting to explain why Jesus' disciples continued preaching after His death.
D. Because the theory depends entirely on the Gospel accounts while rejecting the historical sources outside the Christian tradition.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson argues that the substitution theory came later and conflicts with earlier Christian and non-Christian testimony about Jesus’ crucifixion.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — approx. 08:15–10:59

Q15. Why does the lesson consider the question "Is the Bible true?" important to the Christian?
A. Because the Bible contains more historical information than every other ancient document.
B. Because the Bible is the oldest religious document available to Christians.
C. Because the Bible is the standard for Christian belief, so questioning its origin and validity raises a question about the foundation of the faith.
D. Because the Bible must be confirmed by archaeological discoveries before Christians can accept its teachings.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the Bible is the standard for belief, so questions about its origin and validity affect Christian faith.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 00:29–01:14

Q16. What confidence does the resurrection of Jesus give believers about their own future?
A. It gives believers confidence that they will avoid physical death if they maintain their faith until the end.
B. It gives believers confidence that they will rise again because Jesus Himself rose from the dead.
C. It gives believers confidence that they will experience resurrection only if they have never struggled with doubt.
D. It gives believers confidence that physical death has already ceased to exist for everyone who believes in Jesus.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents Jesus’ resurrection as assurance that believers will rise too.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — 04:03–05:46

Q17. What does the lesson highlight about the different backgrounds of the Bible's authors?
A. Their different backgrounds show that the books developed from several unrelated salvation stories.
B. Their different backgrounds suggest that the books were written independently without a common theological direction.
C. Their different backgrounds mean that the books reflect different understandings of salvation that cannot be brought together.
D. Their different backgrounds show that, despite their differences in countries, classes and professions, their writings form a unified salvation story.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson highlights that authors from varied backgrounds contributed to a unified salvation story.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 01:14

Q18. Why was the flood understood as an act of preservation as well as judgment?
A. The corruption of humanity had become so extensive that intervention was necessary to preserve the human race
B. Humanity had become incapable of receiving God's forgiveness and therefore needed to be completely destroyed
C. God needed to demonstrate His authority before establishing His covenant with Noah
D. The flood was primarily intended to punish those who had rejected Noah's preaching
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents the flood as an intervention intended to preserve the human race amid extensive evil.
REF: THEODICY III — approx. 01:49–04:16

Q19. What did the scapegoat represent in the Day of Atonement picture presented in the lesson?
A. It represented the animal whose blood was brought behind the veil to make atonement for the high priest.
B. It represented the one upon whom the sins and rebellious acts of the Israelites were placed before being sent into the wilderness.
C. It represented the high priest who entered the Most Holy Place and returned to announce that the sacrifice had been accepted.
D. It represented the people of Israel who remained outside the tabernacle while the high priest offered sacrifices for their sins.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the scapegoat carried the Israelites’ sins away into the wilderness.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD I — 11:18–12:55

Q20. Why does the lesson consider the time interval between an original document and the earliest surviving manuscript?
A. Because the age of the surviving manuscript determines whether its original author was inspired by God.
B. Because a longer interval between manuscripts automatically makes the original document historically unreliable.
C. Because the date of the surviving manuscript determines whether the document's message is doctrinally correct.
D. Because the interval helps us consider how close the surviving evidence is to the period in which the original was written.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson uses the interval to assess how close surviving manuscripts are to the original documents.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 01:37–02:26

Q21. What pattern of divine intervention is identified throughout Scripture?
A. God intervenes whenever His people experience suffering for an extended period
B. God intervenes primarily in ways that advance His overarching will and purpose
C. God intervenes only when human beings have exhausted their own ability to solve a problem
D. God intervenes whenever evil becomes visible enough for humanity to recognize it
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson describes God’s interventions as advancing his overarching will and purpose.
REF: THEODICY III — approx. 00:16–01:49

Q22. What were the differences found in the approximately 5% that did not match in the Isaiah comparison?
A. They involved major changes to the story and theology presented throughout the book of Isaiah.
B. They involved spelling differences, omitted letters and misspelled words that did not change the core meaning.
C. They involved entire sections of Isaiah that had been removed from the later manuscript tradition.
D. They involved different accounts of the life, ministry and death of Jesus within the book of Isaiah.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson characterizes the differences as spelling and copying errors that do not change the core meaning.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 04:02–05:04

Q23. What does Christ's resurrection change about the way death is understood?
A. Death remains the final outcome of human existence but is no longer something Christians should fear
B. Death is no longer the final word for those who belong to Christ because resurrection gives hope beyond physical death
C. Death is removed from the experience of every believer who exercises sufficient faith
D. Death becomes spiritually beneficial because every Christian is guaranteed immediate resurrection after physical death
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents resurrection as hope that death is not the end for believers.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — 04:03–05:46

Q24. What does the lesson say Christianity would become without the resurrection?
A. Christianity would become a less effective form of Christianity because its moral teachings would remain unchanged.
B. Christianity would become a mere religion because the resurrection is what distinguishes the Christian faith from a system of moral teaching.
C. Christianity would become a historical movement because the teachings of Jesus would still provide a complete path to eternal life.
D. Christianity would become a different form of Judaism because the death of Jesus would still fulfil the purpose of the Christian faith.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the risen Savior, rather than moral teaching alone, distinguishes Christianity.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — 06:27–07:18

Q25. What is the main difference between internal and external evidence in the lesson?
A. Internal evidence examines the Bible's own testimony, while external evidence looks to material outside the Bible to see whether it confirms or denies that testimony.
B. Internal evidence examines the Old Testament, while external evidence examines the New Testament and the events surrounding its development.
C. Internal evidence examines archaeological discoveries, while external evidence examines the prophecies contained within the biblical text.
D. Internal evidence examines Christian belief, while external evidence examines whether non-Christians accept the Bible's historical claims.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes evidence drawn from within the Bible from evidence outside it that may confirm or deny its testimony.
REF: IS THE BIBLE TRUE I — 06:41; IS THE BIBLE TRUE II — 00:15–01:10

Q26. What is the lesson's main historical objection to the Islamic substitution theory?
A. The theory emerged several hundred years after Christianity and conflicts with earlier Christian and non-Christian testimony concerning Jesus' crucifixion.
B. The theory emerged before the earliest Christian accounts and therefore represents a competing eyewitness tradition concerning Jesus' death.
C. The theory was based primarily on Roman records that the Christian writers deliberately excluded from their accounts of Jesus.
D. The theory agrees with the earliest historical testimony about Jesus but differs from later Christian interpretations of His death.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson argues that the substitution theory came later and conflicts with earlier testimony about Jesus’ crucifixion.
REF: DID JESUS RISE FROM THE DEAD II — approx. 08:15–10:59

Q27. What is the central purpose of the concept of theodicy as presented?
A. To demonstrate that every form of suffering has an immediately identifiable purpose
B. To defend the goodness and justice of God in response to objections arising from evil
C. To establish that evil exists independently of God's sovereignty
D. To explain why human beings are morally responsible for every form of suffering
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents theodicy as addressing objections to God’s goodness and justice in light of evil.
REF: THEODICY I — approx. 02:11–04:19

Q28. What is the basic claim of the ontological argument as explained in the lesson?
A. God is the greatest possible being, and such a being cannot exist only in the imagination but must exist in reality.
B. God is the first cause of the universe, and therefore everything that exists must ultimately depend on Him.
C. God is the intelligent designer of nature, and the complexity of creation demonstrates that He exists.
D. God is the source of objective morality, and therefore universal moral values demonstrate His existence.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents the argument that the greatest possible being cannot exist only in the imagination and must exist in reality.
REF: IS THERE A GOD III — approx. 06:00–09:51

Q29. Why does Christ's incarnation matter to the question of suffering?
A. God entered human experience and personally experienced hunger, temptation, rejection, suffering and death
B. God entered human experience primarily to demonstrate that suffering is necessary for spiritual maturity
C. God entered human experience so that He could understand human beings despite previously being separated from them
D. God entered human experience to demonstrate that divine power could completely eliminate suffering during earthly life
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Christ experienced human pain and temptation, so God is not portrayed as detached from human suffering.
REF: THEODICY IV — approx. 11:12–12:28

Q30. What is the broader purpose of studying apologetics according to the conclusion of the lesson?
A. To equip Christians with enough intellectual arguments to win debates and demonstrate the superiority of Christianity over every opposing belief.
B. To help Christians replace simple faith with intellectual certainty so that difficult questions about Christianity no longer need to be asked.
C. To equip Christians to understand why they believe, engage their minds with their faith, defend it reasonably, and help others come to Christ.
D. To prepare Christians to become academic scholars who can provide technical answers to every philosophical objection against Christianity.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents apologetics as preparing Christians to reason about and defend their faith and to help others come to Christ.
REF: IS THERE A GOD III — approx. 10:36–15:41
